speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about supporting offenders to mend family ties.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: To aid in their family reintegration, SPS works with community partners to provide family programmes to inmates, and befriending and other pro-social support to ex-offenders after release.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas asked about creating greater acceptance for ex-offenders and recruiting more volunteers to help with rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Yellow Ribbon Project's (YRP) outreach has generated high awareness and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Based on a 2022 survey, about 91% of respondents were aware of YRP's objectives, rehabilitation challenges faced by ex-offenders and the need to reduce stigma towards them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: SPS and YRSG have expanded roles and training for volunteers in areas of in-care and aftercare, including support for families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Collectively, SPS and YRSG have more than 4,000 volunteers supporting rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In 2023, YRSG will focus on showcasing inmates and ex-offenders' talents and contributions to reiterate that ex-offenders can contribute to society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about allowing desistors to perform at National Day Parades (NDPs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We have been providing desistors with opportunities to showcase their talent at public events.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: The Yellow Ribbon Performing Arts Centre Alumni Band had performed at Red Dot August at the Esplanade for the past three years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas asked about alleviating the impact of incarceration on one's family.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In 2023, we will strengthen support for inmates' families by collaborating with more community resources, such as religious organisations, Social Service Offices (SSOs) and Family Service Centres (FSCs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked for a review of the Registration of Criminals Act on spent offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: From time to time, MHA reviews the spent regime for criminal records.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In our last review in 2021, we assessed that the existing regime continues to be appropriate to facilitate the reintegration of ex-offenders, in particular those who committed minor crimes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This position took into consideration the many initiatives to facilitate reintegration and reduce long-term recidivism.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked about support for female ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: RAHWH provides gender-responsive interventions and facilitates social reintegration for the residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to support female ex-offenders and facilitate their reintegration.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Next, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked about collaboration with the Malay/Muslim community to better support inmates and ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I will now speak in Malay about our community's crucial role.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, many Malay/Muslim Organisations (MMOs) have stepped forward to work with SPS and CNB to prevent offending and re-offending by providing support to inmates, ex-offenders, and their family from incarceration to post-release.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These include AMP, FITRAH, Jamiyah, PERGAS, PPIS, PERTAPIS, Yayasan MENDAKI and a number of mosques.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: FITRAH has developed a values-centric in-care religious programme for inmates and prepares Friday Prayer sermons that are contextualised to their rehabilitation needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, all mosques are familiar with FITRAH's work and refer them to FITRAH for support, such as befriending.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Many MMOs have joined Singapore's efforts in supporting rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MHA recognises that there is value in coordinating all these efforts to create greater synergy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Since its launch, many collaborations have been forged.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, FITRAH has collaborated with New Life Stories to develop a referral system where they can tap on each other's expertise.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Jamiyah Halfway House has collaborated with the West Mosque Cluster to further support the reintegration of its residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Supporting inmates, ex-offenders and their family is an endeavour that cannot be undertaken by the Home Team alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: I am thankful to MMOs for working closely with us to uplift and make a difference to the lives of our beneficiaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Your efforts and contributions have helped to keep the recidivism rates low and the number of new drug abusers stable.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: (In English): Sir, in conclusion, thanks to our Home Team Officers, Singapore remains safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to work with our community partners to combat terrorism, prevent drug abuse and support our inmates and ex-offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, we have a war against scams on our hands.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Sitoh Yin Pin asked for an update on the Government's efforts to combat scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I chair the Inter-Ministry Committee on Scams, which leads a multi-agency effort to develop a systems wide collective shield to protect us from scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We deploy a multi-layered defence strategy against scams: first, we endeavour to block scam calls, SMSes, online listings and websites; second, we secure Government services and banking channels; third, we strengthen our enforcement capabilities; and lastly, we strengthen our laws.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Mr Vikram Nair asked how the Government partners industry and people sector stakeholders to combat scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the use of technology in our efforts to fight scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Home Team has established partnerships across Government, private and people sectors, using technology to aid our efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For calls, SPF works closely with local telecommunication companies to terminate mobile lines used for scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2022, more than 6,500 such mobile lines were terminated.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF also engaged WhatsApp on more than 22,800 WhatsApp lines believed to be used in scams in 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For SMSes, the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) mandated SMS Sender ID registration from January 2023 and implemented anti-scam filters to detect potential scam SMSes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under the Sender ID regime, all non-registered senders are flagged as "Likely-SCAM".

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: After a transition period, SMSes carrying unregistered Sender IDs will be blocked upfront.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To address scams arising from international numbers, IMDA is exploring offering the option to members of the public to not to receive international calls and SMSes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For online listings, SPF partners social media companies and e-marketplaces to remove suspicious accounts and advertisements.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2022, more than 3,100 accounts and advertisements suspected of involvement in scams were removed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For websites, SPF uses analytic tools to identify and block scam websites, by detecting tell-tale characteristics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2022, about 20,000 scam websites were blocked.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Home Team also works with stakeholders to secure Government services and banking channels, so scammers cannot exploit system vulnerabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have onboarded all Government agencies onto the SMS Sender ID registry, making Government agencies harder to spoof.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are considering measures that allow the verification of incoming calls from Government officials.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF also deepened their partnership with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and domestic banks to flag and freeze suspicious accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Over the past year, MAS worked with the Association of Banks in Singapore, or ABS in short, on the following measures: (a) a cooling-off period for provisioning new digital tokens; (b) removing clickable links from official emails and SMSes; (c) lowering default transaction limits; and (d) an emergency self-service "kill switch", allowing customers to suspend their accounts quickly if compromised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The MAS and the ABS are exploring a "money lock" solution, which enables customers to "lock up" a designated sum in their bank accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This reduces the amount that could potentially be lost to scams via digital transfers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Derrick Goh spoke about the increased use of foreign payment gateways.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As more foreign gateways open up, we are also working with MAS to review and enhance the suite of anti-scam measures to mitigate the risk of these channels being used for illicit purposes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, investment scams and job scams, which contributed to the bulk of monies lost to scams in Singapore, are very hard to tackle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have, thus, strengthened our enforcement capabilities, to minimise the number of victims and amounts lost to scammers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Anti-Scam Command was formed last year to consolidate expertise in combatting scams across the SPF.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Vikram Nair asked about our collaborations with foreign law enforcement authorities to address the transnational nature of scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF works closely with their foreign counterparts to exchange information and conduct joint operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In 2022, this led to the successful take-down of 13 syndicates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF arrested more than 70 people based overseas, who were responsible for more than 280 scam cases.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza also asked about MHA's plans to reduce the prevalence of money mules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We intend to tighten the law against those who facilitate the movement of scam proceeds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, the vast majority of money mule investigations do not result in prosecution.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Given the evolving landscape of scams, new forms of scams will emerge.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the processes in place to inform and activate stakeholders to address the latest scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Once we are aware of an emergent scam, the SPF works with the media and other stakeholders to publicise information on it so that the public can be put on guard.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF also taps on its partnerships with sectoral stakeholders to swiftly activate a multi-layered defence, which we adapt as the scam evolves.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The best defence against scams is a vigilant and discerning public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To defend ourselves and our loved ones, we need to move beyond awareness, to mobilise every citizen to take action against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked how the Government is keeping up our public education efforts to prevent scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In September 2022, we expanded the ScamShield app to Android device users.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ScamShield protects users by blocking calls from known scam numbers and filtering out potential scam SMSes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I encourage all citizens to download and use the ScamShield app.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By playing your part in reporting scam calls, SMSes, and WhatsApp messages, you protect others by enabling the Police to detect scam messages and fraudulent WhatsApp accounts much more quickly and to put these scam messages on a blacklist.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Derrick Goh spoke about potential levers to ensure co-operation and accountability with stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Last year, we launched the E-commerce Marketplace Transaction Safety Ratings (TSR), a consumer advisory that reviews and tracks the transaction safety of major e-commerce marketplaces based on specific metrics.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The TSR encourages marketplaces to deter and detect scams committed on their platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It allows consumers to make informed decisions on where to do their online shopping safely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will be refreshing the platform ratings in the TSR in April.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Murali Pillai referred to his previous suggestion for SPF to publish the amounts seized and returned to victims.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF does not actively track the cumulative dollar value of assets recovered and the amount returned to victims.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond being aware and acting against scams, we need to educate the public on the consequences of engaging in scam activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Derrick Goh asked about our efforts and partnerships to address the increase in youths involved with scams and to encourage positive youth development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A key initiative for youths is the biannual Delta League, run by SPF and NCPC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Youth participants engage in sports and participate in crime prevention activities, which enhance their awareness of the consequences of crime.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More than 1,200 youths participated in the most recent Delta League which engaged participants in activities that educated them on scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: SPF also issues mid-year and year-end advisories to students and parents through schools to remind students to steer clear of crime, including being alert against attempts to trick them into becoming money mules.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The SPF will continue to work with its stakeholders to promote a sense of social responsibility among our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah suggested having a one-stop unit to assist scam victims and address their financial and emotional needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Victim Care Cadre programme under the SPF provides support to crime victims.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where needed, the Police activate volunteer Victim Care Officers, or VCOs, who work with the Police Psychological Services Department to provide psychological first aid.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Where necessary, the VCOs will also direct victims to available community and professional resources for longer-term psychological support and/or financial support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This includes Family Service Centres, Samaritans of Singapore and the hospitals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah spoke about disabled scam victims, and deaf persons in particular, getting timely help.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Crime victims have multiple avenues for reporting, including online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If a report is lodged in person, the Police buildings are designed to be accessible for persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And if needed, sign language interpreters will be engaged to assist.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will now address a question on the working hours of security officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas asked if the Government would take the lead to regularise their hours, by requiring shorter shift hours for all Government security contracts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Since 2020, it has been mandatory for public agencies to adopt outcome-based contracts for procuring security services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, kindly allow me to say a few words in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   We are fighting a war against scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They prey on our natural human needs and motivation, such as desire for companionship or additional income to support our families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For example, compliant residents may be targeted by scammers impersonating Government agents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The scammers may also target those who are impulsive in nature and create an artificial sense of urgency and require the victims to transfer money and provide information promptly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In cases of love scams or fake friend calls, scammers normally take time to cultivate a close relationship with the victim, gaining their trust before draining their bank accounts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These victims not only suffer financial losses, but also often feel guilty or betrayed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are hurt deeply emotionally and may even have difficulties to trust others in future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As with modern military weapons, the design of scams takes the form of innovative disguises meant to target our needs and desires.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The traps they set up are everywhere, and every day, we find ourselves barraged by various scams.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We must remain vigilant and never let our guard down.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, everyone has a part to play to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While the Government will step up measures to protect us against scams, we need to remain alert and ready to keep ourselves and our loved ones safe.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond exercising individual responsibility, let us also look out for and support others in our community, to strengthen our collective resilience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together, we will be able to fight the war against scams.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Just some clarification questions for Minister pertaining to my cut on new citizen selection which would come under the ambit of the ICA.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The first clarification I have is the point about sensitivities.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think Minister shared that countries-specific information is not put out because it can be misinterpreted, I believe that is what the Minister said.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, the countries that are covered – Malaysia, China, India, Indonesia, Europe, USA, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and other Asian countries – this information that is already provided.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, what specific sensitivities is the Minister referring to when the Minister says that revealing countries-specific information could be misinterpreted?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: My third clarification is on the refreshed Singapore Citizenship journey that Minister spoke of.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Very recently, the former Minister for Foreign Affairs in Singapore, Mr George Yeo, spoke of suggestion of new citizens being approved by a jury of ordinary Singaporeans and these are his comments: "We are completely self-interested.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, we bring in clever people, wealthy people, connected people.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: But some of them when they come in, they think they are a blessing to Singaporeans and act as if we should be pleased that they are here.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I met some of them when I was a Member of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Now, this psychology is very important that Singaporeans do not feel that the foreigners whom we bring in are lording over them and looking down on them and misbehaving." In this regard, Minister said that the content of the refreshed —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Singh, could you get to your question?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Yes, I am putting my question across now, Mdm Chair.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And in this context, with regard to the refreshed Singapore Citizenship journey, Minister shared that the content was co-created with Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can I just confirm with the Minister, which aspect of the content is she referring to?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He asked what aspects of our immigration information is not broken down by specific countries.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I believe if you look at the reports to do with annual awards of Permanent Residency and Singapore Citizenship, we speak of the regions from which the new citizens, as well as the new PRs, originate from.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Is he advocating a position, or he is merely asking a question?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I believe it would be helpful, so I would advocate for it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I used the peg of the findings of the latest Census report which spoke of English and how commonly it is spoken in Singapore, comparing 2020 to 2010, and it is much more widely spoken today.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, the peg that I am coming in from is its utility as a tool to improve integration between Singaporeans and new citizens.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, in that regard, given the new information that we have, I believe it could be a helpful tool to improve integration.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, what sensitivities apply with regard to not wanting to release that information on a yearly basis, when I see it releases its information on PRs and citizenships awarded that year?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not have anything new to add to the previous explanations that had been provided.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And I would think a test need not be applied.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thirdly, on the ground, every day we meet with residents who cannot speak a word of English.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not think anyone would suggest that they are any less integrated to Singapore society.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As to some of the comments he made about applicants who may lord it over Singaporeans and so on, I am not sure what the question is, perhaps I could ask him to repeat it.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Singh, please keep it succinct so that others will have a chance to also ask their clarifications.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The question was with regard to the point that Minister made in her speech about the refreshed Singapore Citizenship Journey.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And she mentioned that the content was co-created with citizens.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, I have asked what aspect of the content was co-created by citizens.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I do not have the details of those content.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if the Leader of the Opposition is interested, we could share it with them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Singapore Citizenship Journey includes materials that are shared with the applicants to our citizenship.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And they can look at these materials in order to be more familiar with Singapore history and culture.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Those probably have involved other citizens in terms of their development.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And there is also, if I recall correctly, a component of the Singapore Citizenship Journey that takes these applicants to various locations.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Those are materials that we can provide to you.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: One on scams, one on cannabis and one on technology.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My experience on the ground is, in terms of scams, it happens very, very quickly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Within a span of three weeks, I have had two separate families come and see me.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And what they shared with me is that, through many money mule accounts in Singapore, money is transferred from account to account, and then transferred out.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And while they are interested in prosecution of those involved in this, they are most concerned with the recovery of the money.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I listened very carefully to the Minister of State Faishal's response, and I thank him for that.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Would it be useful to share with the public the long-term societal harm of recreational cannabis use?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And I use Washington state is a good starting point.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I am not saying it has worked well or negatively there, but it is the 10th year anniversary of Washington state's legalising recreational use of marijuana.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I think it did so in December 2012.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, if we can have some statistical, empirical, evidential data on what the societal effect, the effects on society are – employability, mental health, family relationships, long term – then, we will be on firmer standing on our zero-tolerance to drugs.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr de Souza, can you ask your clarifications?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: My humble suggestion is that that does not substitute the need for good human ground judgement, in order to know how to prevent crime and also disperse crowds.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I am speaking up very much in favour of the retention of best-in-class, world-class officers on the ground to do their job, and not an over-reliance on technology.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As noted by Mr Christopher de Souza, what happens often is that the original sum of monies from the customer's bank account gets dismantled, dispersed and then, goes through the banking system into various other bank accounts not owned by them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And guess how many accounts the original sum of monies went through?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That was how quickly bank accounts were set up and the monies is dispersed through the banking system.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And that is why it is important that we work with the various retail banks to have the retail banks co-located together, so that we can share information quickly and for the banks to quickly trace the monies and close off those bank accounts and stop the monies from moving through the banking system, and then, out of Singapore, whereby it is then out of our jurisdiction.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Indeed, we have been studying the effects and we also have been sharing some of these through our various platforms, including our #CNB Perspective Series.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And essentially, if you look, for example, in the US, for those jurisdictions where cannabis is legalised, you see that the prevalence of cannabis consumption is significantly higher in these states, compared to the overall average.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Another part is, we can also see the more adverse effects, in terms of the medical and health perspective, and also the number of emergency visits and treatments that have been required.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These are things that we continue to follow because we are convinced of the harmful effects of drugs, including cannabis, and we want to share a lot more of these with our people.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In fact, in the coming months, I am going to share – through my social media platforms – some of the perspectives that we know, that we have learnt from our counterparts overseas, who may have a different stance on drugs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And I thank the Member for believing in this; and we really, really appreciate your support.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ultimately, we will still need officers who have the judgement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We need officers who understand our cultural context and our operating conditions, in order that they will be able to put the technologies to good use.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if you compare it to the size of HTX today, which is about 1,500, that is still a 25% increase simply to build the capabilities to use technology more effectively.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is a question of where we are deploying our talent resources in the sense of using technology as a force multiplier.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is still the approach that we hope to take in order to serve Singaporeans better, in order to protect Singaporeans through the use of technology in the appropriate way and also to do so in such a manner as not to overly strain our resources.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: Can the Minister of State share more about it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Essentially, if you look at it, drugs in the body can enter oral fluid, the saliva, through passive diffusion from blood or may be deposited in the oral cavity during oral, smoke or intranasal administration.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, indeed, drug metabolites also can be detected in saliva.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Then, the saliva test, I have shown Members earlier: you need to swab a person's tongue, using the test kit to obtain minute sample of saliva.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The test kit subsequently will check the saliva for controlled drugs and produces results in about eight to 10 minutes.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is similar to the COVID-19 test kits where the test kit will produce red lines if particular drugs are present.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Nevertheless, we will also have a double check.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That means, if we find that there are some test results which are positive, we will bring them back to do further testing.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
text: And I understand her response is that the Government has implemented security outcome-based contracts for all of their security contracts.

speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas
text: My clarification is whether, in precisely these security outcome-based contracts, whether the Government can implement higher weightage for bid proposals that propose shorter working hours for security officers for these two reasons: first, it has been shown that when security officers work shorter hours, they are operationally more effective, which is an outcome in and of itself; and the second is to support the overall effort to better the working conditions of our outsourced workers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We want to improve the working hours, the working conditions for our security officers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, what we are trying to do now is that we want to work with stakeholders to look at outcome-based driven approaches and we do know that the industry actually needs time to also develop expertise, because we are talking about a better match between manpower with technology, and also with the solutions that are available.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will take into account the suggestion that the Member has made.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will go back and look into it and see how the Government agencies can further drive initiatives on this front.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Because, in the example that Minister of State Sun provided, which is consistent with the example that was given to me by the residents who spoke with me, was that: from one account, it goes to six accounts, it goes to 36 accounts and carries on.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, if that algorithm or pattern is recognised by the bank internally, then my humble question is, ought not the bank then be given the power to "kill switch" the transmission of monies from accounts to accounts, without the incumbency being on the consumer, on the customer, but the bank itself.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As I mentioned, the seven major retail banks are co-located with each other and the sole purpose is to be able to exchange information quickly, once they are aware that a scam has occurred, that the victim has lost money.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But the reason I use the example was to demonstrate the complexity.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Because of the proliferation of the number of bank accounts that are being created by money mules who are negligent in the way they have given up control of their bank accounts or some have given up their Singpass IDs to allow others to set up bank accounts, many of these bank accounts are being used to launder these proceeds.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And the banks do need time to be able to trace the monies and activate the "kill switch", as the Member also said.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is something that the banks are working on.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The banks are working closely with the SPF to do that within an hour, to freeze the accounts so that there is a higher chance that we can prevent the monies from going out of the system, so that we can return those monies to the victims.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I just want to pick up on the point on international scams.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I do not know whether it is Minister or the Senior Minister of State, but of the number of scams that are routed internationally, what percentage would that be and how effective are we in capturing these and recovering proceeds?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think you mentioned a number of about 70 people have been arrested, but what percentage is that of the bigger pool?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Not all foreign law enforcement agencies conduct their operations the way we do.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They may face very specific challenges in their home countries, cities or villages.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And that is something that we do not have control over.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But where we can, it is definitely our desire to work with the foreign law enforcement agencies and after they find out who the perpetrators are, they conduct those raids, they inform us.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Sometimes, they are able to recover some portion of the scam proceeds, because you can imagine that the scam proceeds actually move very quickly in the system, even if you were to trace them to Country A, which was where the scam proceeds first go to, you never know how those scam proceeds then find its way to other countries or to other parts of the banking system.

text: Mr Murali, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

text: But I also would like to extend my appreciation to hon Second Minister and the two hon Ministers of State for their responses and outlining their strategies to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: And I am sure the hon Members who join me in wishing them well in their respective missions.

text: With that, Mdm Chairman, may I seek leave to withdraw the cut?
